items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Klein, and you’re right. I didn’t think about that but it’s true.

ctx.x: Right. So then when you got in it it was more integrated, then it went the other way.

Yeah. I think you’re talking about — what you’re talking about is the Tommy Dorsey era, the fallout of the Paul Whiteman band. That’s the thing. Paul Whiteman was a white band. And the King of Jazz and all that stuff, and we know he wasn’t of course but a lot of those musicians ended up being premier studio musicians in the thing — Jimmy Dorsey, Tommy Dorsey, Klein, and you’re right. I didn’t think about that but it’s true. And anyways —
Well you’re writing, you say you’re doing an awful lot more writing now.
